summary: Iteration 3 — RightPolicy branding refresh + new two-vertical Hero + em-dash/copy cleanup. Backend: 25/25 pytest cases pass (health, inquiries, policy-uploads, claim-support + admin auth/me/lists/stats/PATCH/download). Bulk em-dash and copy edits to /app/backend/server.py did not break any JSON responses. Frontend hero verified: testids hero-card-advisory + hero-card-claim render, H1 reads 'Two ways to feel truly insured.', eyebrow chip 'Insurance Advisory & Claim Support' present, hero-talk-advisor-button opens AdvisorDialog ('Book a Free Consultation'), hero-upload-policy-button opens UploadDialog, hero-claim-support-button opens ClaimSupportDialog. /logo.png renders in navbar (data-testid navbar-logo-img), footer, and admin dashboard. Favicon links point to /favicon.png and /favicon.ico in index.html (verified). Em-dash audit clean across /, /services/{health,motor,life,business,travel,personal-accident}, /claim-support — no U+2014 anywhere. Banned phrases ('human-first', 'real humans', 'real people') NOT found anywhere. WhatsApp float (whatsapp-float) visible. Service detail and ClaimSupport pages render correctly. ONE CRITICAL REGRESSION: /admin/login renders blank because AdminLoginPage.jsx uses <Logo/> without importing it ('Logo is not defined' runtime error). Admin dashboard itself works when token is injected directly — so logo migration there succeeded; only the login page is broken.

ui_bugs.issue: Missing import — page uses <Logo asLink={false} className="h-10" /> but never imports Logo. React throws 'Logo is not defined' at /admin/login. Page renders BLANK. Admin cannot log in via the UI at all (only direct API call works).

Still contains the phrase 'Reviewed by humans, not algorithms.' — the iteration 3 brief asked to remove overuse of 'human' / 'real humans' across components. Suggest 'Reviewed by experienced advisors, not algorithms.'

action_items: CRITICAL: Add `import Logo from "@/components/site/Logo";` to /app/frontend/src/pages/AdminLoginPage.jsx (currently missing — admin login UI is fully broken/blank).
MINOR: Replace 'Reviewed by humans, not algorithms.' in /app/frontend/src/components/site/PolicyReview.jsx with experienced-advisor copy to fully complete the iteration-3 wording cleanup.

(House-keeping done by tester) /app/backend/tests/test_rightpolicy_api.py had 3 stale tests calling public GET /api/inquiries and /api/policy-uploads which are admin-only since iteration 2; updated to use admin token. No product change.

Hero.jsx still imports ShieldCheck from lucide-react and uses it as a decorative icon (Option-1 card + chip). That is correct (the brand mark is the new Logo component); no action needed.
Logo component (Logo.jsx) renders ; clean and reused in Navbar, Footer, AdminDashboardPage. AdminLoginPage was missed.
server.py CORS: allow_credentials=True with allow_origins='*' remains technically invalid per the CORS spec (carried over from iter-2). Non-blocking for this iteration.
AdminDashboardPage.jsx is ~763 lines (>700 guideline) — consider splitting per-tab components. Carried over from iter-2; non-blocking.

Em-dash sweep is complete: no U+2014 in /app/frontend/src or /app/backend/server.py (verified by grep). Banned-word sweep is complete except the single 'humans' occurrence in PolicyReview.jsx noted above.
Favicon: index.html correctly points to /favicon.png (rel=icon, apple-touch-icon) and /favicon.ico (rel=shortcut icon); both files exist in /app/frontend/public.
updated_files: /app/backend/tests/test_rightpolicy_api.py (3 stale tests migrated from public GET /api/inquiries|/api/policy-uploads to admin-authenticated /api/admin/* — product code untouched)

rca of the issue: AdminLoginPage.jsx blank screen RCA: the iteration-3 commit replaced the inline ShieldCheck-with-text wordmark in AdminLoginPage with a <Logo /> component, but did not add `import Logo from "@/components/site/Logo";`. AdminDashboardPage.jsx received the same migration AND its import (line 15), confirming the omission was localised. Reproduction: open /admin/login → blank page; pageerror 'Logo is not defined'; React reports 'An error occurred in the <AdminLoginPage> component.' Mitigation: add the single import line. No backend or data implications.
